paragraphs: Many people in Dublin city have no driveway. They park on the street near their home. To do this, they buy a parking permit from the council.
In January, the price will go up by 30 per cent. A one-year permit will cost €65, not €50. A two-year permit will cost €105, not €80. It is the first rise in more than 15 years.
After that, the price will change every year with the cost of living.
Parking meters will also cost a little more. In the busy city centre, one hour will cost €4.20, not €4. The council also wants lower speed limits on almost all city roads.
sentZh: 都柏林市很多人家裡沒有車道。
他們把車停在家附近的街上。
為此，他們向市議會購買停車證。
一月起，價格將上漲30%。
一年期停車證將收65歐元，而不是50歐元。
兩年期停車證將收105歐元，而不是80歐元。
這是15年多來第一次漲價。
之後，價格每年都會隨生活成本而調整。
停車計時收費也會稍微貴一點。
在繁忙的市中心，一小時將收4.20歐元，而不是4歐元。
市議會也希望幾乎所有市區道路都降低速限。

paragraphs: Dublin City Council will raise the cost of residents' parking permits by 30 per cent in January. It is the first increase in more than 15 years. The permits allow people who live on pay-and-display streets, often without a driveway, to park outside their homes.

A one-year permit will go up from €50 to €65, and a two-year permit from €80 to €105. After that, the price will go up or down each year in line with the Consumer Price Index, which measures inflation.

The council says permit prices have not changed since 2011, while hourly parking charges on the same streets rose by 30 per cent. Today, 12 hours of parking in the busiest zone costs about the same as a full year's permit.

Parking meter prices will also rise. In the yellow zone, which includes the city centre, an hour will cost €4.20 instead of €4. Last year, councillors rejected a plan for permits of up to €225 a year.
Councillors will hear about the changes on Tuesday, along with a plan to lower speed limits on almost all city roads.
